subject: general
question: The '80-pillar hall' was part of the palace of which great emperor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The remains of the famous **80-pillar hall** were discovered at **Kumrahar**, located about five kilometers from **Patna** (ancient **Pataliputra**) in **Bihar**.
 
• This monumental structure is attributed to the **Mauryan Empire** and served as a grand assembly hall or part of the royal palace of **Emperor Ashoka**, who reigned from **268 BCE to 232 BCE**.
 
• Archaeological excavations at the site were conducted by **Dr. D.B. Spooner** between **1912** and **1915**, which brought to light the existence of these massive monolithic pillars.
 
• The hall was constructed using **Chunar sandstone**, and the pillars exhibited the distinct **Mauryan polish**, a technique that gave the stone a mirror-like, metallic luster.
 
• The layout consisted of **80 columns** arranged in **eight rows of ten pillars each**, reflecting the advanced engineering and architectural capabilities of the **3rd century BCE**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Ashoka is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mauryan Architecture and Pataliputra:**

 
 
• **Megasthenes**, the Greek ambassador sent by **Seleucus Nicator** to the court of **Chandragupta Maurya**, provided a detailed account of the city and the palace in his book **Indica**.
 
• He described the palace as more magnificent than the Persian palaces of **Susa** and **Ecbatana**, noting its wooden fortifications and grand stone pillars.
 
• Historical evidence suggests that while the pillars were stone, the roof and floor of the **80-pillar hall** were made of **wood**, which is why much of the structure perished due to fire and environmental factors over **2,000 years**.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Foreign Styles:**
 
 
• Scholars often note a resemblance between the **80-pillar hall** and the **Achaemenid** architecture of **Persia**, specifically the **Hall of a Hundred Columns** at **Persepolis**.
 
• However, the **Mauryan** pillars were **monolithic** (carved from a single stone), unlike the Persian pillars which were constructed in segments.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Kumrahar:**
 
 
• The site of **Kumrahar** is not only famous for the hall but also for other findings like the **Arogya Vihara** (an ancient hospital-monastery) and the **Anand Bihar**.
 
• These findings highlight **Pataliputra** as a major center for administration, religion, and healthcare during **ancient India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Rulers Mentioned:**

 
 
• **Samudragupta** and **Chandragupta I** belonged to the **Gupta Dynasty** (ruling roughly between **319 CE and 540 CE**). Their architecture focused more on early **Hindu temples** and **cave shrines**, such as the **Udayagiri caves**.
 
• **Harshavardhana** (reigned **606 CE to 647 CE**) was a ruler of the **Pushyabhuti Dynasty** with his capital at **Kannauj**. His era is noted for the support of **Nalanda University** rather than the 80-pillar hall of Pataliputra.
 
 
 
• **Technical Features:**
 
 
• The pillars of the hall were approximately **10 meters** in height and were buried deep into the ground to provide stability for the massive structure above.
 
• The use of **stone** for royal buildings was a transition from the earlier extensive use of **timber** in the **pre-Mauryan** era.
